messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] zero branchlength
parts:
Hi -- the tree cannot have polytomies, nor can it have zero-length branches or negative-length branches. You can check for these by visualizing the tree, using APE's is.binary (IIRC) to check that the tree has no binaries, load the tree and look at the $edge.length variable, etc.

Cheers,
Nick

Hi -- this got away from me, this tree has a lot of problems.  Summary of what I figured out below. Apologies for the ranting, I was going very quickly, as stuff like this takes chunks out of my day.  If you can get past the ranting, and work through the code, you will find it useful.

Cheers, Nick 


SUMMARY RECOMMENDATION:

1. *MAKE SURE* you understand basic phylogenetics, Newick files, and APE before attempting more advanced stuff like BioGeoBEARS

2. This page is the one you want for typical tree file problems:

Testing and Fixing Common Tree File Problems In BioGeoBEARS
http://phylo.wikidot.com/testing-for-fixing-common-tree-file-problems-in-biogeobears

3. Go back to your *original* dated tree, and try working through #2 with that, remembering to save the output to a new Newick file, and then use that new Newick file in the BioGeoBEARS run.

Cheers,
Nick


# Details, with mini-rants (sorry!)


library(ape)
trfn="/drives/GDrive/z_help/2018-01-30_Uzma/beast_tree2.newick"
tr = read.tree(trfn)

# This says you have no negative-length branches
sum(tr$edge.length < 0)

# But this says you have 4 very short branches:
sum(tr$edge.length == 0)
TF = tr$edge.length == 0
(1:length(tr$edge.length))[TF]

# And when we look at the branchlengths, they are zero!
nums = (1:length(tr$edge.length))[TF]
tr$edge.length[nums]

# Find the nodes:
trtable = prt(tr, get_tipnames=TRUE, printflag=FALSE)

# Oops, this tree has other BIG problems. 

# Not all the tips come up to 0!  time_bp=time before present, only one tip has time 0!

# Number of tips in tree
ntips = length(tr$tip.label)

trtable$time_bp[1:ntips]

I'm extremely sorry about the last email and the tree file...actually this is not my study, someone's else and this tree is not created by me,  and she just wanted me to run this analysis on my laptop , therefore I don't know much about how it looks like but yes when I got zero branchlength probelm then I tried to fixed it with *1000  but as I don't know about other issues with this tree that's why again I got the same error and I have to ask you about that if you could see...again sorry! But for sure...I know some basic phylogenetics!

Thank you for detailed answer, I really appreciate!
Best,
Uz
On Tuesday, January 30, 2018 at 3:42:33 AM UTC+5, Nick Matzke wrote:

Hi -- this got away from me, this tree has a lot of problems.  Summary of what I figured out below. Apologies for the ranting, I was going very quickly, as stuff like this takes chunks out of my day.  If you can get past the ranting, and work through the code, you will find it useful.

Cheers, Nick 


SUMMARY RECOMMENDATION:

1. *MAKE SURE* you understand basic phylogenetics, Newick files, and APE before attempting more advanced stuff like BioGeoBEARS

2. This page is the one you want for typical tree file problems:

Testing and Fixing Common Tree File Problems In BioGeoBEARS
http://phylo.wikidot.com/testing-for-fixing-common-tree-file-problems-in-biogeobears

3. Go back to your *original* dated tree, and try working through #2 with that, remembering to save the output to a new Newick file, and then use that new Newick file in the BioGeoBEARS run.

Cheers,
Nick

library(ape)
trfn="/drives/GDrive/z_help/2018-01-30_Uzma/beast_tree2.newick"
tr = read.tree(trfn)

# This says you have no negative-length branches
sum(tr$edge.length < 0)

# But this says you have 4 very short branches:
sum(tr$edge.length == 0)
TF = tr$edge.length == 0
(1:length(tr$edge.length))[TF]

# And when we look at the branchlengths, they are zero!
nums = (1:length(tr$edge.length))[TF]

trtable = prt(tr, get_tipnames=TRUE, printflag=FALSE)

On Monday, January 29, 2018 at 4:36:10 AM UTC+5, Nick Matzke wrote:
Hi -- the tree cannot have polytomies, nor can it have zero-length branches or negative-length branches. You can check for these by visualizing the tree, using APE's is.binary (IIRC) to check that the tree has no binaries, load the tree and look at the $edge.length variable, etc.

Cheers,
Nick
